permutation_test.finding: No source reached (including 4 independent academic papers that quote the working paper's methods) specifies what is permuted, what is held fixed, or the permutation count. Only confirmed: a permutation null exists and combines the five features into a single statistic/score.
permutation_test.disambiguation: Not the same design as Gomez-Cram's confirmed activity-matched event-level sign-flip null — different paper, do not assume equivalence.

composite_construction.finding: Combines 5 inputs into a single statistic/score; aggregation method (weighted sum / rank / fitted model) and weight source (estimated vs assigned) not found anywhere reached.
composite_construction.flagged_unreliable_figure: A 25%/20% weight split surfaced during search with no corresponding source snippet across the entire result set — treated as unsourced/likely fabricated, not carried forward.

component_definitions.directional_concentration: named only; HHI-style measures found in citing papers are those papers' OWN features, not confirmed as Mitts & Ofir's definition
component_definitions.pre_event_timing: named only, no window length or anchor point found

profitability.finding: computed retrospectively on resolved markets, using the actual realized outcome — NOT out-of-sample. Structurally adjacent to (not confirmed identical to) this project's own selection-circularity concern.

within_vs_cross_trader.finding: Flags specific (wallet, market) pairs as anomalous based on that wallet's own multi-factor profile; explicitly contrasted against market-level tools (ILS family) in the same sources. Not positioned as a real-time "copy this trader" tool by any source — explicitly described as unsuited to real-time use given profitability's resolution-dependence.

controls_and_limitations.finding: "cannot observe the full portfolio of any given trader"; "cannot rule out... unlikely coincidental patterns rather than genuine exploitation of material nonpublic information" (Harvard blog); profitability's resolution-dependence independently characterized as a real-time-deployment limitation by 2 academic sources.

papers.contradictions_with_project_citations: NONE — all previously-cited headline figures (69.9% win rate, >60 SD, ~$143M, 210,000+ pairs, Iran case study) independently corroborated by 4 additional academic sources in this pass.

randomized_direction_null.unit: EVENT level (all of a trader's trades within one event get one shared Rademacher ±1 sign flip)
randomized_direction_null.explicit_rationale_for_event_level: trade-level randomization would overstate independent bets by splitting one position into many trades; market-level would incorrectly split correlated same-event positions into separate bets
randomized_direction_null.statistic: mid-p estimator (Lancaster 1961; Routledge 1994) of realized PnL vs simulated-PnL distribution, chosen to handle discreteness/ties
randomized_direction_null.contradicts_project_citation: project cited 10,000; primary text says B=1,000 throughout, '10,000' does not occur in the paper

pinning_floor_handling.project_own_problem: 0.00067 p-value floor at 1,500 reps, 12.5% of traders pinned
pinning_floor_handling.paper_approach: truncates p-values at the combinatorial bound [2^-(E+1), 1-2^-(E+1)] given E events; chose E>=10 specifically so 2^10=1024 > B=1000, making event count (not simulation count) the binding resolution constraint
pinning_floor_handling.note: no analogue in the source paper to compare this project's 12.5%-pinned diagnostic against

minimum_event_counts.unit_mismatch_note: project's M>=10 threshold is in POSITIONS, a different unit; not confirmed equivalent
minimum_event_counts.robustness: E>=4 or no filter gives an IDENTICAL classified set to E>=10 (only denominator changes, combinatorial bound makes <4-event accounts unable to reach p<0.05 regardless)

split_half_method.split_type: RANDOM draw of each trader's EVENTS into training/test — explicitly NOT calendar-time
split_half_method.explicit_paper_rationale: market conditions (user base, event types, liquidity) vary substantially over the sample period; random split ensures both sets span the full period and share a comparable user base
split_half_method.persistence_figure_definition: P(classified skilled in test | classified skilled in training) — a CONDITIONAL TRANSITION PROBABILITY, not a population share
split_half_method.secondary_statistic: PnL rank correlation train->test: 0.11 overall, -0.12 among training-set winners (profit partially reverses); p-value rank correlation: 0.35 overall
split_half_method.bearing_on_project_own_test: instr_v7 uses a TEMPORAL split (not random-event) and reports a two-group comparison (not a train->test transition probability) — two independent axes of difference, both now precisely characterized. Pass 3's 'NOT DIRECTLY COMPARABLE' verdict confirmed and sharpened, not overturned.

population_3pct_figure.population: all Polymarket, markets created after 2023-01-01, resolved by 2025-12-31
filters: market-maker exclusion by behavior (>=100 markets traded, >=70% volume from limit orders, both sides of an outcome in >=70% of markets) -- 0.10%/1,660 accounts excluded before classification
p<0.05 two-tailed, NO multiple-testing correction in headline spec
population_3pct_figure.exact_result: 54,325 accounts = 3.16% of all 1.72M accounts (contradicts project's cited 3.14%, see headline_contradiction)
population_3pct_figure.gap_vs_project_26.1pct: project's own pool classified 26.1% skilled, an order of magnitude above even the paper's most permissive reported specification (4.8%) -- unlikely explained by filter strictness; most likely a population/denominator difference. Flagged as an open item for the project's own population definition, not resolved by this pass.

multiple_comparisons.headline_spec: NO correction, explicitly acknowledged (~5% false-positive rate expected under the null by construction)
multiple_comparisons.robustness_check: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, applied separately per tail (skilled tail, anti-skilled tail)
multiple_comparisons.bh_corrected_result: skilled share drops from 3.16% to 1.95% of all accounts at the >=10-event filter
multiple_comparisons.robustness_of_substantive_results: price-discovery/persistence results shown robust across both corrected and uncorrected classifications (Appendix Table B.1)

independence_claim.refinement_found: <1% for humans, <4% for bots (secondhand, refines project's existing human-only framing)
independence_claim.unreliable_figure_flagged: rho~=0.13 (implying ~1.7% shared variance) surfaced via one AI-summarized blog fetch, inconsistent with the <1% claim, not corroborated elsewhere -- not incorporated

execution_measure.benchmark_F_definition: per-(market,token) volume-weighted average price (VWAP), BUY-side trades only, computed from the full resolved trade tape
execution_measure.circularity_finding: CONFIRMED STRUCTURALLY SIMILAR to this project's own 'partial and endogenous' fair-price benchmark problem. Paper's own intro argues prediction markets 'solve' the shared-benchmark artifact problem (citing Fama 1972, Anand et al. 2012) but this only holds for the directional leg (W is benchmark-free); the execution leg's F is itself trade-tape-endogenous, the same category of problem the paper's intro criticizes elsewhere.
execution_measure.analytical_note_flagged_as_inference: F enters both components with opposite sign (W-F and F-P), so measurement noise in F would mechanically induce a negative correlation between the two measured components -- not sourced from the paper, this pass's own derivation, unresolved without the paper's actual robustness section

earliness_finding.access: ordinary secondhand only, not found in author's own repo
earliness_finding.operational_definition: UNRESOLVED -- not found anywhere reached: unclear if 'entering' means first trade, largest trade, or size-weighted average; unclear anchor (market close vs resolution vs underlying event date)

A_permutation_test_equivalent_to_placebo.what_a_future_project_version_must_do: construct its own activity-matched placebo from scratch (instr_v6/match_control()) rather than inherit any protection from Mitts & Ofir's design, per Pass 5's original defensive assumption -- now confirmed necessary rather than merely cautious.
